name: Irony
overview: Scripture reveals irony as a powerful rhetorical device used to expose hypocrisy and unbelief, often highlighting the contrast between human pride and divine truth. For example, the Pharisees and Herodians ironically acknowledge Jesus as a true teacher who does not show partiality, yet they oppose Him (Matthew 22:16). Similarly, the Roman soldiers mockingly hail Jesus as "King of the Jews" while inflicting suffering upon Him (Matthew 27:29), and Pilate's inscription above Jesus ironically proclaims His kingship even as it serves as a charge against Him (Matthew 27:37). These instances demonstrate how irony underscores the tragic blindness of those who reject God's revelation while unwittingly affirming His authority.
